title: Stacked machine learning on cfDNA fragments separates malignant from benign ovarian masses
summary: Low-pass whole-genome sequencing of plasma cell-free DNA from 743 participants supplied four fragmentomic feature classes (fragment size, nucleosome footprint, copy number, repeat elements) to a stacked machine-learning model. Trained on one cohort with cutoffs fixed there, it reached AUCs of 0.930 (internal test) and 0.932 (external test). Adding CA125 and HE4 raised AUCs to 0.964 in both and specificity from 77.9% to 88.4% and from 78.9% to 91.5% at sensitivities of 88.4% and 89.2%. The authors call for prospective evaluation.
